title: The Last-Level Branch Predictor
problem: Server workloads suffer from high branch misprediction rates in state-of-the-art 64KB TAGE-SC-L predictors, wasting 3.6-20% of execution cycles (9.2% average). Large branch working sets and hard-to-predict branches remain challenging despite decades of predictor research.
motivation: Improving branch prediction accuracy in server workloads can significantly enhance processor performance and reduce wasted execution cycles.
method: The Last-Level Branch Predictor adds high-capacity backing storage to the baseline TAGE predictor, exploiting the insight that branches requiring longer histories span multiple program contexts (call chains). The system predicts upcoming contexts and prefetches the associated branch metadata into a small in-core buffer, which is accessed in parallel with the unmodified TAGE predictor.
key_novelty: Using program context locality to organize branch prediction metadata in a hierarchical structure with predictive prefetching into a high-speed in-core buffer.
contributions: Introduces LLBP microarchitecture that adds high-capacity backing storage without modifying the baseline TAGE predictor
Demonstrates that grouping branches by program context significantly reduces metadata storage requirements per context
Achieves 0.5-25.9% MPKI reduction (8.9% average) using 512KB backing storage behind 64KB TAGE-SC-L
primary_theme: hierarchical branch prediction with context-aware prefetching
